result:
The final answer of 4 is not supported, and I believe it is wrong.

The proposed solution counts maximal simple colorings only for n = 1, 2, 3 and then assumes the count stays at 4 for all n ≥ 2. The 3×3 example it relies on fails. Take the coloring where (1,1), (1,2), (2,2) are white and all other cells are black. The rectangle with rows 2–3 and columns 1–3 has corners (2,1), (2,3), (3,1), (3,3), all black. The ant can walk its boundary: (2,1) → (2,2) → (2,3) → (3,3) → (3,2) → (3,1) → (2,1). It passes the white cell (2,2) straight, and it turns only at black corners. So this coloring is not simple, and the 3×3 family the solution claims is invalid. Its later analysis of larger grids also stays at the level of unverified guesses, so nothing justifies extending the count to 2024.

I did not derive the correct value of the count for the 2024×2024 grid, so I cannot give the right answer. The reasoning does not support 4.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
